data.name: Oshina
data.gender_notes: Oshina is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Oshina is the goddess of fertility, agriculture, and the harvest. She is often depicted as a nurturing mother and protector of life. The name Oshina carries the meaning “Goddess of fertility” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Oshina usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of fertility and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes abundance, growth, and nurturing energy.
data.etymology: Oshina belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of fertility.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Oshina total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

In agricultural communities, the goddess Oshina is invoked during planting and harvesting seasons to ensure a bountiful yield. Oshina festivals and rituals are an integral part of rural life, bringing the community together in shared devotion and thanksgiving for the blessings of nature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Oshina holds profound spiritual significance as a symbol of the nurturing and protective aspects of the Divine. It represents the cyclical nature of life and the power of the forces of nature to sustain and replenish. For Hindus, the goddess Oshina embodies the essence of Mother Nature and the fertile, productive potential within each person. The name is a reminder of the interconnectedness of all living beings and the importance of honoring and respecting the natural world.
